name: CA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Josh Harder has a large financial advantage ($4.7M cash vs $19K)
District leans Democratic by 8 points on the partisan baseline

model.rationale: Harder combines incumbency, an eight-point Democratic district lean, and an overwhelming fundraising edge against a barely funded challenger, while both major prediction markets price him around 98%. The fundamentals-based margin of roughly 20 points stands with little evidence to move it.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Harder or an unexpectedly strong Republican turnout environment could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Josh Harder, the Democratic incumbent in CA-09, faces Republican John McBride in the general election. The district leans Democratic by about eight points, and Harder holds a massive financial advantage, with roughly $4.7 million on hand compared to under $20,000 for McBride, who has raised only about $52,000. No outside groups have meaningfully engaged on either side.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price Harder's chances near 98 percent, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the lopsided money picture, all pointing to a comfortable Harder win.
